messages:
samir: quick check — running paged-attn + flash fusion microbench on 8xA100 (4x GPUs per job), seq_len=8192, batch=4. seeing ~15% tail latency spike on a subset of runs after kv-cache warms up. anyone hit something similar? attaching sample log below.

olivia: which commit/branch? opfusion-main or your local patch?

samir: opfusion/bench-fuse branch (PR still draft). command I ran: `./run_bench.sh --model llama-13b --seq 8192 --batch 4 --fusion on --kv-cache`

dana: can you paste the exact env + kernel flags? curious if prefetch or fp16 path differs. also try `KERNEL_FUSE=0` to see if fusion is the culprit.

samir: env: `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3`, `OMP_NUM_THREADS=4`, `ENABLE_PREFETCH=1`, `FLASH_ATTENTION=on`. logs: ```[run 12] median=18.2ms p95=27.1ms p99=45.3ms  (sudden p99 jump around iter 80-85) stacktrace shows kernel launch queue growth```

maria: I can spin a canary on dedicated pool (dedicated-gpu-8). happy to run a stable vs branch A/B if you give me the script and commit hashes.

samir: thanks — pushing results as soon as I reproduce with `KERNEL_FUSE=0`. also ping @olivia for a quick CR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/opfusion/pull/312 (bench harness + small opt). PTAL if you have a minute.

olivia: saw the PR, will skim now. initial thought: the fused attention kernel introduces extra kernel launches for split pages at boundaries — can you add logging for page boundary counts? that might correlate with the spike.

dana: also try `ENABLE_PREFETCH=0` — prefetching sometimes overlaps and clogs the SMs for long sequences. if spike disappears, we know it's a scheduling/cuda-stream issue.

samir: running three variants now: (1) baseline main, (2) opfusion/bench-fuse with KERNEL_FUSE=0, (3) opfusion/bench-fuse with ENABLE_PREFETCH=0. will post perf table.

eng-bot: perf-run scheduled: job=bench-2035501234-1 on pool=dedicated-gpu-8, ETA ~12m. logs will be at https://ci.redwood/bench/2035501234 when done.

maria: I've queued a longer run (200 iters) to catch the tail behavior. leaving the canary pinned to avoid autoscaling noise.

samir: quick paste of interim numbers (iter 0-50): baseline p99=42ms, opfusion(KF=0) p99=43ms, opfusion(prefetch=0) p99=37ms. early signs prefetch might be relevant but need full run.

olivia: interesting — if disabling prefetch helps, maybe the fusion path has an ordering dependency with KV eviction. can you also capture NVTX ranges or `nvprof --print-gpu-trace` for the failing window?

samir: will capture NVTX and full `ncu` timeline for the iter 70-90 window where spikes show up.

dana: small ask: add a quick check in the harness to flush KV cache between batches for the test; that'll confirm if residual state is amplifying the issue.

samir: good idea. I'll add `--flush-kv-between-batches` flag and re-run.

maria: if results point to fusion ordering, we should prioritize a small fix to guard the boundary kernel launch. I'll hold off larger experiments until we confirm.

samir: thanks all — will post final numbers + nvtx dump here. tagging this for follow-up in tomorrow sync if we don't resolve: @olivia @dana.
